senses.gloss: f.(b. h.; בקע)cut, notch, whence valley, plane; a group of fields; v. בָּאגִא; esp. a short cut for farm-laborers &c.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Tahorot 6:7">Toh. VI, 7</cite>, a. e. <he>הב׳ בימות החמה וכ׳</he> the path through the fields in summer-time (when used by field laborers) is considered as private ground with regard to Sabbath laws, as public with regard to levitical purity.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 61b:9">B. Bath. 61ᵇ</cite> when one sells … a field <he>בב׳ גדולה</he> within a large group of fields (all belonging to the seller).
Ib. (in a place) where they call לשדה ש׳ ולב׳ ב׳ a field sadeh and an estate bikah; a. fr.—Trnsf. an unguarded field, moral danger.

<cite ref="Eruvin 6a:4">Erub. 6ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Eruvin 100b:6">100ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Chullin 110a:2">Ḥull. 110ᵃ</cite> <he>רב ב׳ מצא וכ׳</he> Rab found an unguarded field and fenced it in, i.e. found people transgressing the law in ignorance and instituted preventive regulations.—Pl. <he>בְּקָעוֹת</he>.

senses.gloss: (constr.) בִּקְעַת pr. n. pl. Valley of—, as ב׳ יזרעאל, ב׳ ידים &c., for all of which see the respective determinants.
